subtype: Giving feedback that can be used [Response]
passage:
Dear Farhan,
Thank you for sending the deck this morning. The customer story on slide three is the strongest part: the delayed-parcel example made the problem clear to me in ten seconds. One thing to change: on slide seven the sales chart has no label on the vertical axis, and someone in the room will ask what the numbers mean before you can make your point. Could you add the label and one line saying what the chart shows? Then people will not lose the thread. I am free tomorrow at ten if you would like me to look again. You are close. 🙂
Kishore

qa.q: Which slide has the chart with no label on the vertical axis?
qa.a: Slide seven has the sales chart with no label on the vertical axis.

qa.q: What does Kishore want for Farhan by offering to look again tomorrow?
qa.a: Kishore wants Farhan to feel supported and able to act, and the closing line "You are close" shows encouragement instead of criticism.

qa.q: What could Farhan do first after reading the letter?
qa.a: Farhan could add a label to the vertical axis on slide seven and a one-line takeaway, then send the deck back to Kishore for a second look.

qa.q: How might Farhan feel reading this compared with a comment like "Not good enough"?
qa.a: Farhan would probably feel respected and clear about the next step, since one strong part and one exact spot with a reason leave little to defend.

grounding: Shows a reviewer naming what works, pointing to a concrete spot and giving the reason in a kind, timely note.

subtype: Giving feedback that can be used [Response]
passage: Same day, always. If I wait a week, the person has already made up a story about my silence. So when a junior sends me a report, I read it once for what works and say that first, honestly. This time it was the clean summary table. Then I pick one spot, page four, the paragraph with three numbers and no source, and I say why: a reader will doubt the rest if they cannot trace it. I suggest adding a source line. Then I stop. Sangeeta, you asked if it feels awkward. A bit. But when they come back with the fix and a question, I know it landed. Shankar

qa.q: Which page has the paragraph with three numbers and no source?
qa.a: Page four has the paragraph with three numbers and no source.

qa.q: How does Shankar feel about giving feedback, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Shankar feels a little awkward but sure of the approach, saying it feels awkward yet judging by the juniors who come back with the fix and a question that it lands.

qa.q: What makes Shankar's feedback something a junior can act on?
qa.a: It names what works first, points to one concrete paragraph, gives the reason and suggests a fix, all on the same day.

qa.q: What might the junior who sent the report feel if Shankar waited a week to reply?
qa.a: They might make up a story about the silence and expect the worst, which is why Shankar replies the same day.

grounding: Shows a reviewer who gives specific, timely, kind feedback with a named strength, one concrete spot and a reason.
